A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CLIPDrag, with matching core methods and DRAGBENCH experiments. Text, equations, figures and tables support comparison throughout. v1 ends after its references; v2 additionally contains readable Appendices A–F.

before.justification: v1 reports original qualitative editing results, quantitative DRAGBENCH comparisons and ablations of text guidance, gradient fusion and point tracking in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds baseline comparisons, sequential-guidance and conflicting-instruction experiments, and measured inference times in its appendices.

M1.justification: The stated motion-supervision objective in Equation (5) gains an L1 latent-preservation term outside an optional mask and explicitly specifies L1 feature matching. LoRA adaptation, gradient fusion and fast point tracking remain unchanged. Masks already appear in v1 Figure 5, so the revised objective does not establish that masking capability or its underlying implementation is newly introduced.

E1.justification: DRAGBENCH remains the dataset, and text-drag and pure drag editing remain the principal tasks. Appendix D adds a distinct input scenario involving deliberately conflicting text and drag instructions. Additional baseline results otherwise extend evaluation within existing coverage.

E2.justification: The text-drag comparison expands from DragDiffusion, FreeDrag and DiffCLIP to include InstantDrag, LightningDrag, RegionDrag and StableDrag in Figure 10. Pure drag evaluation adds FastDrag and StableDrag to the previous DragDiffusion comparison. Figure 12 also evaluates sequential guidance alternatives, and Table 3 introduces a runtime comparison including SDE-Drag.

E3.justification: Existing training settings, IF/MD metrics and the five pure-drag iteration caps remain unchanged. New experiments vary guidance order and text strength, and Appendix F measures average inference time over 100 sampled DRAGBENCH examples. The strongest conflicting-instruction setting is inconsistent: Figure 13 labels it λ = 50, whereas Appendix D says λ = 100.

E4.justification: The existing text-signal, fusion and point-tracking ablations are retained. Appendices B–D add substantive controls and failure analyses: more specific prompts with versus without dragging, both sequential guidance orders versus joint guidance, and conflicting instructions under different text strengths. These investigate alternatives and failure conditions absent from v1.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the statement that random seeds and learning rates were adjusted for the point-tracking comparison. Neither reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Averaging the new timings over 100 different images does not introduce repeated-seed uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds baseline scores, qualitative comparisons and failure cases, plus runtime results: Table 3 reports 47.8 seconds for CLIPDrag versus 80.3 for DragDiff. The original CLIPDrag and DragDiff curves in Figure 6 are retained. However, new Table 2 reports CLIPDrag fidelity of 0.94 and 0.93 at 20 and 40 iterations, whereas Figure 6 in both versions shows 0.93 and 0.91. These conflicting entries do not establish a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: Equation (5)'s mathematical loss definition is revised to specify L1 norms and include preservation of latent values outside mask M. The other principal equations and mathematical reasoning are retained; no new theorem, proof or formal guarantee is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims: combining text and drag signals resolves complementary control weaknesses, global-local supervision integrates them, and fast point tracking improves convergence. Additional comparisons support these retained claims without substantively redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly explains how sequential editing can invalidate handle or target locations and preserve an incorrect editing direction. Appendix D makes the expectation of consistent instructions explicit and describes neutralization, ambiguity and implausible outputs when guidance conflicts or becomes too strong. These add meaningful applicability boundaries to v1's mainly positive discussion.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link, documents optional generation of the original-image prompt by a captioning model such as GPT-4V, and specifies a single 3090 GPU for timing measurements. Section 4.1's main implementation hyperparameters remain unchanged. The PDFs establish disclosure of a code link, not independently verified repository availability.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands and revises research positioning through new diffusion-model background and method-specific discussions. Added works include InstructPix2Pix, SINE, FlexiEdit, Null-text Inversion, LightningDrag, InstantDrag and RegionDrag, with an explicit comparison to concurrent RegionDrag. Several earlier citations, including DragNoise and SmartBrush, disappear.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in related work, accompanied by an organized appendix, a revised title and affiliations, acknowledgments, explanatory footnotes and small language corrections. Most of the abstract, introduction, method exposition, existing experiment narrative and conclusion remain closely matched; the main section sequence is retained.

P2.justification: v2 revises Figure 1's sculpture examples and instructions, expands Figure 6 with additional curves and legends, and adds Figures 10–14 and Tables 1–3. The new tables partly redisplay existing results alongside added comparisons. Most other original figures are retained and repositioned, rather than newly generated evidence.

improvement.justification: The added sequential-guidance controls and conflicting-instruction analysis address previously untested alternatives and failure conditions. Broader comparisons, measured timings and a code link also improve assessability. These benefits are tempered by new reporting inconsistencies: Table 2 conflicts with Figure 6 on CLIPDrag fidelity, and Appendix D conflicts with Figure 13 on text strength. The later paper provides useful additional evidence and qualifications, but these reliability issues limit the overall gain.
